Additional Comments: The patient, a 58-year-old postmenopausal woman, has a history of left breast cancer diagnosed in March 2017, characterized as Stage IIb (T2N1M0) Grade 2 Invasive Ductal Carcinoma (IDC) that is estrogen receptor-positive (ER+), progesterone receptor-positive (PR+), and HER2-negative. She underwent a left lumpectomy and sentinel lymph node biopsy, revealing residual IDC with lymphovascular invasion and positive margins, necessitating a re-excision. Postoperative MRI indicated suspicious enhancement, but subsequent biopsy showed benign proliferative fibrocystic changes. Genetic testing for BRCA was negative. The patient experiences mild, intermittent left breast pain post-surgery and has concerns about cosmesis and hair loss during chemotherapy, for which scalp cooling has been discussed. She has supportive family and friends nearby and is preparing for her niece's event in February.
